categories.main_business_segments: Texas Roadhouse, Inc. operates three primary restaurant concepts: Texas Roadhouse (moderately priced, full-service, casual dining focused on steaks and American fare), Bubba’s 33 (full-service, casual dining with burgers, pizza, wings, and a sports-bar atmosphere), and Jaggers (fast-casual, focused on burgers, chicken, and salads). The company also has a retail and licensing segment, but its reportable segments are Texas Roadhouse and Bubba’s 33.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes freshly prepared, high-quality food using proprietary recipes for consistency and taste. Steaks are hand-cut daily on-premises, and side items and rolls are made from scratch in each restaurant. Digital enhancements include online ordering, waitlist management, contactless payments, and kitchen display systems to improve efficiency and guest experience.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Texas Roadhouse serves a broad segment of consumers seeking high-quality, affordable meals in a casual, family-friendly environment. Key customers include families, groups, and individuals looking for dine-in or to-go options. Bubba’s 33 targets sports fans and casual diners, while Jaggers appeals to fast-casual and drive-thru customers.
categories.geographic_coverage: As of December 2023, the company operated 741 restaurants (635 company-owned and 106 franchised) across 49 U.S. states and ten foreign countries, including significant presence in Texas and Florida. International franchise locations are in countries such as the Philippines, South Korea, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE.
categories.supply_chain_position: Texas Roadhouse operates at the downstream end of the supply chain, directly serving end consumers through its restaurant locations. The company manages procurement directly with suppliers and relies on a national distribution company for food and beverage delivery to its restaurants.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding the restaurant base domestically and internationally, acquiring franchise locations, maintaining high restaurant-level profitability, leveraging scalable infrastructure, and enhancing the digital guest experience. R&D efforts focus on menu innovation, operational efficiency, and digital technology enhancements to improve service and throughput.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily from restaurant food and beverage sales at company-owned locations. Additional revenue streams include franchise royalties and fees, retail product sales, and management services for certain franchisees. Gift card sales and breakage also contribute to revenue.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Texas Roadhouse competes in the highly competitive casual dining segment against national and regional chains, independent restaurants, fast-casual and quick-service brands, and meal kit/grocery alternatives. Key competitors include Outback Steakhouse, LongHorn Steakhouse, Chili’s, and Applebee’s. The company positions itself as a value leader with a focus on quality, service, and a unique atmosphere.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Texas Roadhouse reported total revenue of $4.63 billion, up 15.4% year-over-year, with net income of $304.9 million. The company opened 30 new company restaurants and acquired 8 franchise locations, with comparable restaurant sales growth of 10.1%. The company maintains a strong balance sheet, significant cash flow from operations, and continues to invest in growth and shareholder returns.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Texas Roadhouse differentiates itself through its commitment to 'Legendary Food, Legendary Service,' offering freshly prepared, high-quality meals at attractive price points in a fun, welcoming atmosphere. The brand emphasizes hand-cut steaks, made-from-scratch sides, attentive service, and a unique dining experience with local flair, setting it apart from competitors in the casual dining space.
